purpose: Teach: 見捨て/テック/送り出し/王家/シリアル/樽/鍛える/野心

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、お互いを、絶対、見捨てないって、若い頃、誓ったよな、覚えてる?本気で、これは、絶対の、約束だ、絶対。
lines.en: Gran — do you remember? We swore it when we were young. That we'd never abandon each other. No matter what. It's an absolute promise.
lines.style: Slow, measured opening. Voice softens on her name. Weight behind 'swore'—this matters. Gentle but certain. Trailing off slightly as if watching for recognition in her face.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん。最近のテック、本当に、便利よね、私、年寄りには、ちょっと、難しいけれども、新しいこと、覚えるの、楽しいわよ、本当に。
lines.en: Yes. Technology these days is really so convenient. It's a bit tricky for someone my age, but learning new things—it's genuinely fun.
lines.style: Warm, clear voice. Opening brightness on 'yes.' Light energy when she mentions tech being fun. Not wistful, present—she's enjoying this moment. Slight lift at the end.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、孫の送り出し、保育園の前、何度か、立ち会ったよな、ばあさん、覚えてる?懐かしい思い出だ、本当に、本気で、絶対。
lines.en: When we were young, remember how many times I stood with you at the daycare gate, Gran? Sending the grandkids off. Those are precious memories.
lines.style: Soft, almost tender. Slight pause before 'remember'—checking if she's there with him. Voice dips on the memory itself, as if handling something fragile. Quiet conviction on 'precious.'

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、王家の歴史、本、二人で、よく、読んだわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で、感動した話、たくさん、あったわよね、本当に、絶対。
lines.en: And we used to read those books about royal history together, didn't we? So many stories moved us both deeply. Do you remember?
lines.style: Warm, present recall. Slight rise on 'together'—a gentle invitation to join the memory. Her voice carries affection without strain. Quiet wonder underneath, as if rediscovering something she'd forgotten she loved.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 朝食、私たち、シリアル、最近、食べる時、増えてきたわよな、ばあさん、簡単で、便利よね、本当に、年取って、楽な、選択肢、ね、絶対。
lines.en: Breakfast time now—we eat cereal more and more these days, Gran. It's simple, isn't it? Convenient. When you get older, you appreciate the easy choices.
lines.style: Matter-of-fact but not cold. Slight gentleness on 'Gran.' This is observation, not complaint—he's noticing how life changes. Pace is slower, reflective. No bitterness, just quiet acceptance.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 昔の田舎、ワイン樽じゃないけれど、味噌樽、いっぱい、あったわよね、あなた、覚えてる?日本の伝統、本当に、深いわよね、本気で、絶対。
lines.en: Back in the countryside, there were so many miso barrels, remember? Not wine—miso. The traditions of Japan run so deep, don't they?
lines.style: Nostalgic, almost dreamy. Voice softens around the memory of 'miso barrels.' Slight pause as if seeing it. The question isn't really asking—it's inviting him to see it with her. Warm and transported.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、体を、本気で、鍛える時代、覚えてる?ばあさん、私、本当に、頑張ったよな、お前にも、応援、してもらった、感謝、ね。
lines.en: When we were young, remember those days when I really trained hard? You cheered me on, Gran. I'm grateful for that.
lines.style: Quiet gratitude beneath the words. Slight catch on 'cheered me on'—genuine emotion surfacing. Pace is unhurried. Not performing emotion, but letting it be visible. Ends with quiet sincerity.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃のあなたの、野心、本気で、輝いていたわよね、覚えてる?私、本当に、惚れ直したくらいよ、本気で、本当に、絶対、ロマンチックね、本気。
lines.en: Your ambition when you were young—it shone so brightly. I still remember. It made me fall in love with you all over again, truly. That was so romantic.
lines.style: Voice warm and unguarded. Opens with admiration. Soft wonder on 'shone brightly.' The middle section—'fall in love'—is tender and direct, not shy. Ends with gentle certainty, a small smile in the voice.
